newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: SOCCER-IRISH MANAGER RECALLS THREE FOR ICELAND QUALIFIER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-IRISH MANAGER RECALLS THREE FOR ICELAND QUALIFIER.

text.p: David Kelly, Roy Keane and Phil Babb will all make their Republic of Ireland comebacks in the World Cup qualifier against Iceland on Sunday.
Their recalls are Mick McCarthy's only changes to the side who beat Macedonia 3-0 a month ago.
Sunderland striker Kelly, 31 later this month, is the biggest surprise. He returns for his first cap since March last year.
Kelly is only playing in Sunderland's side at the moment because Niall Quinn, Ireland's leading striker, has been ruled out for the rest of the season with knee ligament damage.

McCarthy has pikced him to partner Tony Cascarino in preference to veteran John Aldridge, who still needs one goal to equal Frank Stapleton's Irish record of 20 and will again be a substitute on Sunday.
Liverpool's Babb returns to the Irish three-man central defence in place of injured Aston Villa star Steve Staunton.
And McCarthy confirmed that Manchester United midfielder Keane's own comeback will be as a central defender as well _ but with instructions to step forward into attack as often as possible.

Keane's Manchester United team-mate, Denis Irwin, switches from right to left as a wing-back to the exclusion of Leeds youngster Ian Harte, who has recently been dropped from the first-team at Elland Road as well.
McCarthy said: "There have been some difficult decisions to make, but David Kelly is back because he deserves to be back.
"He has done very well at Sunderland this season and I'm hoping his comeback will be as successful as a few other Irish players' recently.
"I did not want to disturb my midfield trio, who did so well against Macedonia. That is one of the reasons why Roy Keane is playing at the back.
"If he does as well there as I think he will, maybe he'll stay in that position for us for some time to come."
Ireland team: Alan Kelly; Jeff Kenna, Gary Breen, Roy Keane, Phil Babb, Denis Irwin, Alan McLoughlin, Jason McAteer, Andy Townsend, David Kelly, Tony Cascarino
